subject: Clarifying data classification, model-improvement exclusion, and subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Ellen Torres <ellen@terrahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@terrahealth.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data use & subprocessors before final DPA

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft last week. Procurement is reviewing, but Security has a few technical clarifications before we can sign:

1) Training/model improvement: can you explicitly confirm whether customer-provided prompts and generation outputs will ever be used to train or improve Redwood models or any third-party models? We need a firm "no-training" commitment (or a very specific scope/exclusion).

2) Prompt/response ownership: does TerraHealth retain ownership of prompts and outputs? Are there any rights Redwood asserts over derivatives? Please point us to the clause that covers this.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: please provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and clarify whether any of them (or Redwood itself) will transfer data outside the US/EU. If there are transfer paths to countries without adequacy, we need to understand SCC use or alternative safeguards.

4) Evidence: Security has asked for a short evidence bundle: (a) SOC 2 Type II cert, (b) current subprocessors CSV with access scopes, and (c) a short runbook describing how you prevent customer data being used for model training.

Can you respond to these or point us to the redlines that would address them? We are on a tight timeline for our Q2 rollout.

Thanks,
Ellen Torres
Director, Cloud Security
TerraHealth

[Attachment: TerraHealth_Security_Questions_20270311.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Ellen Torres <ellen@terrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data use & subprocessors before final DPA

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, full detail below and attached artifacts.

Summary answers:
- Training/model improvement: Redwood will not use TerraHealth prompts or outputs to improve our hosted model weights unless you explicitly opt in via a contract addendum. We propose the wording in Section 4.2 (attached) for the DPA: "Customer Data will not be used for model training or model improvement of any production models without Customer's prior written consent."
- Ownership: TerraHealth retains all rights in prompts and outputs. Redwood claims no derivative ownership; see Section 3.1 in the DPA draft.
- Subprocessors & transfers: attached is our live subprocessor list (CSV). Most subprocessors operate in the US; when transfers outside the EU are required we rely on SCCs or equivalent contractual safeguards and log residency in the CSV.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and a short ops note about training exclusion are attached.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_redacted_2026.pdf, Redwood_subprocessor_list_2027-03.csv, training_exclusion_runbook.txt

What I propose for next steps:
1) Legal (Neha) to confirm the exact DPA sentence and whether we need a separate addendum for "no-train" vs inlining the clause in the main DPA.
2) I'll share the subprocessor CSV and host a 30-minute call with your security team Friday to walk through the list and evidence.
3) Procurement, if agreeable, can send a PO after a short call.

Would Friday 10:30am PT work for you for a quick walkthrough?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (PDF); Redwood_subprocessor_list_2027-03.csv (CSV); Redwood_SOC2_redacted_2026.pdf (PDF); training_exclusion_runbook.txt (TXT)]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Ellen Torres <ellen@terrahealth.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data use & subprocessors before final DPA

Hi Ellen — looping in legal to be explicit on language. A few notes from Redwood legal: 

- "No-training" commitment: we are comfortable committing that Customer Data will not be used to train production models, and we can include an explicit clause that covers prompt/response content. Proposed clause: "Redwood will not use, access, or analyze Customer Data for the purpose of training or improving AI models or model weights, nor will Redwood allow any subprocessors to do so, except to the extent Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in addendum."

- Ownership: we will add a short paragraph in Section 3 clarifying that all customer-provided content and generated outputs remain Customer Data and that Redwood does not assert derivative ownership nor claim rights to reproduce outputs beyond delivering the service.

- Subprocessors: the attached CSV includes the access scope column — note that some monitoring/telemetry providers receive highly redacted metrics only. For transfers, we will state reliance on SCCs and Customer's option to require EU-residency for processing under a Dedicated/Private deployment option (if residency is an absolute requirement).

Action for Ellen: please flag any language you consider insufficient and we can either inline it in the DPA or create a narrow addendum. If TerraHealth needs KMS/HSM integration or on-prem handling for non-export, we can route you to our Private deployment team for an architecture discussion (that would be a separate commercial conversation).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

On a process note: Jonas — please upload the SOC2 and subprocessor CSV to the secure Drive link and share with TerraHealth security as evidence.

[Attachment: proposed_clause_examples.txt (TXT)]

From: Ellen Torres <ellen@terrahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@terrahealth.com, security-team@terrahealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data use & subprocessors before final DPA

Neha, Jonas — thank you for the quick turn. A few follow-ups from Security and Procurement after reviewing the attachments: 

- The proposed "no-training" sentence is close but Security wants the phrase "including derived outputs and log data" added to ensure telemetry and generation logs are excluded. Can you add "including model-generated outputs, prompt logs, and derived telemetry" to the sentence?

- Procurement requests an annotated subprocessor CSV that makes explicit which subprocessors have access to plaintext Customer Data vs. telemetry-only, and which locations/processors are covered by SCCs. The current CSV is useful but we need the access-scope column normalized.

- We also need your SOC 2 auditor contact or report hash so our team can validate the certificate (redacted copy is okay; ideally a letter from your auditor).

- Minor contract ask: Procurement prefers the no-training commitment in an addendum so it survives future DPA standardization. Please propose an addendum template.

We have a procurement freeze on new vendor deployments until 03/31 unless these items are cleared, so time is tight.

Best,
Ellen

[Attachment: TerraHealth_review_notes_20270315.docx (DOCX)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Ellen Torres <ellen@terrahealth.com>, procurement@terrahealth.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data use & subprocessors before final DPA

Ellen — appreciate the detailed feedback and the timeline heads-up. Plan & next steps: 

1) DPA addendum: Neha will draft a short addendum with the explicit "no-training" language including the "including model-generated outputs, prompt logs, and derived telemetry" text and attach it to the DPA. We'll aim to share the addendum by EOD Thursday.

2) Subprocessor CSV: I've asked ops to normalize the access-scope column; you will get an annotated CSV showing "plaintext access", "telemetry-only", and "no-access" along with country of processing. Expect that by tomorrow morning.

3) SOC2 validation: attaching a notarized/redacted SOC2 summary and contact for our auditor in the Drive link. If you prefer, we can arrange a short call between your security lead and our auditor (15 minutes).

4) Deployment options: If you require EU-residency or HSM-backed encryption, we can provide a Private deployment proposal (pricing and timeline separate). I've added Marissa (solutions) to the thread to coordinate a technical scoping call if needed.

5) Call: can we do 03/18 at 10am PT for the walkthrough and to sign off on the CSV? If that works I'll send an invite.

Thanks again — we'll move fast on all items so you can clear the procurement freeze.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183
